sources.entry: presence by sara-star-quant - Per-repo memory, outcome telemetry, and a calibrated-confidence gate for Claude Code, with MCP and AGENTS.md projections so other AI coding tools can read its context. Notes survive sessions; success claims need test evidence; your reverts are remembered. Local-only, stdlib runtime.

summary.one_liner: presence is a local-only Claude Code plugin that keeps per-repo notes, outcome telemetry, and a confidence gate so later sessions pick up prior context, with read-only MCP and AGENTS.md projections for other AI tools.
summary.what_it_does: It builds and reuses a living model of each repo Claude Code touches, so architecture notes persist across sessions. It tracks commits Claude made and watches for reverts, amends, and PR closes, then surfaces that history in future sessions. It collects file changes, test failures, and build results between turns and shows them at the next prompt. A Stop hook checks whether success claims like "fixed" or "done" are backed by test or build evidence since the change, warns when they are not, and can optionally hard-gate git commit and push. A read-only MCP server and an AGENTS.md adapter expose the same context to other clients. State is stored under ~/.claude/presence/ and is not uploaded.
use_cases: give Claude Code memory of a repo across sessions
track whether committed changes get reverted
require test evidence before accepting 'done' claims
share project context with Cursor, Codex, or Gemini CLI via AGENTS.md
expose project notes to MCP clients like Claude Desktop
enforce commit gates in regulated or high-security setups
how_to_run: Optional: append -s -- --bootstrap to auto-install Python 3.13 via uv
Optional: ./install.sh --build-ext for the Rust fast path
notable: Global install with no per-project setup; four presets from solo-dev to zerotrust
Outcome telemetry tracks reverts and amends of Claude's own commits
Calibrated-confidence Stop hook checks success claims against test and build evidence
Read-only MCP and AGENTS.md projections let Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and others read the same context
Zero-Trust preset adds AES-GCM at rest, tamper-evident audit log, and fail-closed integrity checks
caveats: Windows is not supported directly; the README says to install in WSL2
The README documents CI only on macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64
Optional features (PR status via gh, update check, webhook notifier) make network calls when enabled; they are off by default
Not a compliance certification; the README's disclaimer says it is not a substitute for tests, review, or security review
keywords: stop claude from claiming done without tests
